meta.title: The Runaway Rice Cake
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale with repeated lines

paragraphs: On Saturday evening it rains in Green Hill. Tom, Lily, and Pip are at Grandma's house. Rain runs down the window, and the room is warm. Pip lies on the floor and listens. "Will you tell us a story, Grandma?" asks Lily. "Yes, I will," says Grandma. The story has a song, and Grandma lets the children say it with her.

An old woman makes rice cakes and wishes for a friend. One small cake jumps off the table and runs away. It sings, "Run, run, as fast as you can!" "You can't catch me, I am the rice cake!" A dog appears and runs after it. "Where are you going?" asks the dog. "Run, run, as fast as you can!" "You can't catch me, I am the rice cake!" Tom and Lily say the song with Grandma. Pip lifts his head. He wants to run, too.

Then a hen appears and runs after the dog. "Where are you going?" asks the hen. "Run, run, as fast as you can!" "You can't catch me, I am the rice cake!" Next a fox joins the race. "Where are you going?" asks the fox. "Run, run, as fast as you can!" "You can't catch me, I am the rice cake!" "The fox will catch it," says Tom. "No, I think it will run too fast," says Lily.

The rice cake runs past a dark cave and over a stream. It disappears behind a big tree. While the animals look for it, the fox stands by the stream. He says, "I don't believe you can run so fast." The rice cake comes out and stops to show him. Then the old woman comes with her plate. "Let's share the cakes," she says. All four sit by the stream and eat a piece. Soon the plate is empty. The small cake is lucky, and it hides under a leaf. Grandma ends the story and says, "Now it is time for bed."
